title: Dixieland versus jazz versus ragtime
summary: Jiles explains how Dixieland, jazz and ragtime differ and why ragtime has to be played from written music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: I think it was, it was the last one year wasn't it? Yeah, it was Chris Ballmer. That's who it was. That's who it was. And that it wasn't, in a way they played pretty nice. But I mean as they tried to play ragtime music, Dixieland is two different music. Everybody don't know that. Dixieland and ragtime, ragtime come out before Dixieland. Now Dixieland was a step up to what you would call jazz. That's another different one. Now like the bands around, plays for instance, what would they call the band, what this guy name, the trumpet player that died?

Gerard? George Gerard. Now some people would call them playing Dixieland music. Well that ain't what I would call Dixieland, Dixieland music they playing jazz, that's what they stepped up music, they stepped it up, that was jazz, they come right over and fell from Dixieland to jazz. And after jazz, well they come with the bop and all that you see. Well that's the music, they play like, playing it fast, fast, fast, all that, when they stepped up music. But Dixieland wasn't played like that. It was a set tempo, boom boom, da you know what I mean? I mean that's the jazz, that's not Dixieland. But some people don't know that they put it together, say that's a Dixieland band, I'll have the tramo and all the clarinet, but it's a step up.
But what are you trying to do with this Love, Giles band, or whatever you want to call it?

Well I think that would be a good thing to put back and let the people look back and see, this is what I'm trying to tell you about the difference in the music of Dixieland, jazz, and ragtime. Some people never did hear ragtime music, you know, because it was so complicated that nobody played it. I think that's one of the greatest music going, is rag. I just love it, me and myself.
How do you all play it? I mean I know, but I want you to tell me for the time. How do you get it?

How do we get it? Well we've got the music for it. Playing it from the music because it's not music that you can think, you've got to know it. It's got to be in you, or either you look at the notes and play it. You can't try to put two notes where one goes, not in ragtime. You've got to play it just so. They have numbers that you play in ragtime and they've got times of funeral march in it. Then you'll go to a foxtrot. Then you'll go in a blues time. All that's in one piece. And that's very complicated. That's real, the facts. It's in that music. And any time you can change times and different keys like that, it's really complicated. You can't think of, to do them things and do it on time, you'd have to be a genius. So that's why you have to have the music and keep it all with. And nobody wants to fool you. I could tell those boys from England was trying to play it and they didn't have the music, and that's what would make them jump from the middle and somewhere else, just to make the people understand what they was playing, but so far as the music wasn't there. They'd get you with the music. You take it for that frog there, that's a mess. You play that and make Paul run out of wind.

That's right. And Dixieland, you cut the note short. The faster you play, the more you can think of them. When you're slow and have to hold back and go up high and you come down low it'll mess you up. You've got to know. But fast you can run over it quickly and blot out some of that nobody wouldn't know.
